title: Level statistics in the fractal phase of generalized Rosenzweig--Porter models
authors: Victor Delapalme, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, Alexander K. Hartmann, Marco Tarzia, Davide Venturelli
abstract: The Rosenzweig--Porter (RP) random matrix ensemble has emerged as a minimal model for the integrability-to-chaos crossover in quantum many-body systems. Its phase diagram features a region with fractal eigenstates, exhibiting intermediate spectral and localization properties between the fully localized and fully delocalized regimes. In this work, we explore several generalizations of the RP model and determine their level statistics at the scale of the Thouless energy $E_T$, which characterizes the crossover. Using tools from free probability theory and the replica method, we compute the full counting statistics in the limit of large system size, and show that it takes a simple, universal scaling form around $E_T$, shared across all variations of the model. We validate our analytical predictions using exact numerical diagonalization of large samples, and large-deviation algorithms that resolve the full counting statistics down to probabilities as low as $10^{-40}$. We also contrast our predictions with measurements on the quantum random energy model, which is the simplest model displaying many-body localization.
summary: This paper investigates level statistics in generalized Rosenzweig–Porter models, minimal models for chaos crossover. Using advanced techniques like free probability theory, the authors derive a universal scaling form for full counting statistics in the fractal phase ($1 < \gamma < 2$). The findings confirm universality across model variations and provide deep insights into spectral correlations in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the level statistics within the fractal phase of generalized Rosenzweig–Porter (RP) random matrix models.
main_result: The full counting statistics exhibit a simple, universal scaling form around the Thouless energy ($E_T$), which is shared across various generalizations of the RP model.
method: The authors employ free probability theory and the replica method to analytically compute the full counting statistics in the large system size limit.
model_or_system: The core system is the generalized Rosenzweig–Porter (RP) random matrix ensemble, which models the crossover between integrability and chaos. The Hamiltonian structure involves a diagonal random part ($A$) and a coupling term ($B$), allowing generalizations to Wigner or orthogonally invariant matrices.
key_observables: Full counting statistics, level compressibility, and generalized Inverse Participation Ratios ($I_q$).
important_parameters: The phase is controlled by the parameter $\gamma$, defining regimes: fully delocalized ($\gamma < 1$), intermediate fractal ($1 < \gamma < 2$), and localized ($\gamma > 2$). The Thouless energy ($E_T$) characterizes the crossover.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that level compressibility is a superior diagnostic tool compared to raw level spacings, especially in non-uniform density of states regimes. A key comparison is made with the Quantum Random Energy Model (QREM).
figures_summary: Figure B1 illustrates the rate function $\Phi_N(k)$ for finite $N$ versus the asymptotic limit, confirming convergence properties.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the RP model's phase diagram using advanced statistical tools. It calculates full counting statistics via free probability theory and validates these analytical results through large-deviation algorithms and numerical diagonalization, contrasting findings with simpler models like QREM.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses spectral properties in systems exhibiting intermediate quantum dynamics (fractal eigenstates), which is crucial for understanding the transition between integrable and chaotic regimes in complex many-body Hamiltonians relevant to AMO physics.
